app.help.intro1: Ryewired is a virtual breadboard for building and simulating audio circuits. Drop components onto the board, wire them together, and press Run.
app.help.intro2: Use the Signal Generator, Oscilloscope, and Spectrum Analyzer to see how your circuit affects audio. Try “illegal” connections — the sim will tell you what’s wrong.
app.properties.wiperStaysAdjustable: Wiper stays adjustable while engaged — everything else is locked.

app.properties.emptyState: Select a component or jumper wire to edit its properties

app.permanent.lockedPower: Stop the simulation or bypass the pedal to change Power settings
app.permanent.power.label: Power Supply
app.permanent.power.power_on.label: Power On
app.permanent.power.power_on.hint: Turns the circuit's power on or off, like unplugging the battery.
app.permanent.power.voltage.label: Voltage (V)
app.permanent.power.voltage.hint: The supply voltage powering the circuit — 9V is standard for most pedals.
app.permanent.power.current_limit_ma.hin: The most current the supply can deliver before it can't keep up, like a battery running low under heavy load.
app.permanent.power.reverse_polarity.hin: Swaps + and −, simulating a battery or power adapter plugged in backwards.
app.permanent.power.battery_sag.label: Battery Sag
app.permanent.power.battery_sag.hint: How much the supply voltage dips under load as you play — higher settings mimic a tired battery, audibly compressing and "browning out" on loud playing.
How much the supply's own resistance limits current — higher values make Battery Sag more pronounced.
app.permanent.input.label: Input
app.permanent.input.waveform.label: Audio Source
app.permanent.input.waveform.hint: What signal to feed into the circuit — a test tone, noise, or a real recorded guitar sample.
app.permanent.input.source_impedance.hin: How "stiff" the thing feeding this circuit is, like a guitar pickup's output. Lower values act more like an ideal source that isn't affected by what it's plugged into; a real passive pickup is typically around 6,000–12,000Ω.
app.permanent.input.frequency.label: Frequency (Hz)
app.permanent.input.frequency.hint: The pitch of the test tone. A guitar's low E string is about 82Hz; middle A is 440Hz.
app.permanent.input.amplitude.label: Amplitude (V)
app.permanent.input.amplitude.hint: How loud/hard the input signal hits the circuit — like picking softly versus digging in.
app.permanent.input.dc_offset.label: DC Offset (V)
app.permanent.input.dc_offset.hint: Shifts the whole signal up or down by a fixed voltage. Rarely needed — mainly useful for testing bias-sensitive circuits.
app.permanent.input.phase.label: Phase (°)
app.permanent.input.phase.hint: Shifts where in its cycle the test tone starts. Mostly useful for comparing two signals — won't audibly change a single tone on its own.
app.permanent.input.looping.label: Loop Audio File
app.permanent.input.looping.hint: Restarts the audio file from the beginning when it finishes playing.
app.permanent.input.audio_file.label: Audio File
app.permanent.input.audio_file.hint: Optional. The recorded sample to play through the circuit when Audio Source is set to "Audio File" — has no effect otherwise.
app.permanent.output.label: Output
app.permanent.output.load_impedance.hint: How much whatever is plugged in downstream (an amp, another pedal) "pulls" on this circuit's output. Very high values (1,000,000Ω+) barely affect the sound; lower values can noticeably darken the tone, like plugging into a cheap mixer input.
app.permanent.output.volume.label: Master Volume
app.permanent.output.volume.hint: The overall listening volume — doesn't affect the circuit itself, just how loud you hear the result.
app.permanent.output.mute.label: Mute
app.permanent.output.mute.hint: Silences the output without stopping the simulation.
app.simulation.disconnectedLegMessage: {who}'s {leg} isn't connected to anything — it's the only thing on its row. A {label} with a floating leg can't do anything on a real board, and the voltages here won't mean much until it's wired up.
component.resistor.label: Resistor
component.resistor.resistance.label: Resistance
component.resistor.resistance.hint: How strongly this resistor opposes current flow — higher values let less current through.
component.resistor.power_rating.label: Power Rating
component.resistor.power_rating.hint: The most heat this resistor can safely dissipate before burning out.
component.resistor.tolerance.label: Tolerance
component.resistor.tolerance.hint: How close the real resistor is likely to be to its stated value — a real part is never exact.
component.resistor.failure.over_power: Resistor exceeded its power rating and burned out. Power = V²/R — use a higher wattage resistor or reduce voltage.
component.capacitor.label: Capacitor (Film/Ceramic)
component.capacitor.description: Non-polarized film or ceramic capacitor. Can be placed either way.
component.capacitor.capacitance.label: Capacitance
component.capacitor.capacitance.hint: How much charge this capacitor can store — sets which frequencies it blocks or passes in a filter or coupling stage.
component.capacitor.voltage_rating.label: Voltage Rating
component.capacitor.voltage_rating.hint: The most voltage this capacitor can safely handle before it fails.
component.capacitor.type.label: Type
component.capacitor.type.hint: The capacitor's construction — mainly affects real-world size and cost, not the simulated behavior here.
component.capacitor.tolerance.label: Tolerance
component.capacitor.tolerance.hint: How close the real capacitor is likely to be to its stated value — a real part is never exact.
component.capacitor.failure.over_voltage: Capacitor voltage rating exceeded. Use a higher-rated capacitor.
component.capacitor_electrolytic.label: Capacitor (Electrolytic)
component.capacitor_electrolytic.descrip: Polarized electrolytic capacitor. Stripe side is negative (–).
component.capacitor_electrolytic.capacit: How much charge this capacitor can store — sets which frequencies it blocks or passes in a filter or coupling stage.
component.capacitor_electrolytic.voltage: The most voltage this capacitor can safely handle before it fails.
component.capacitor_electrolytic.toleran: How close the real capacitor is likely to be to its stated value — a real part is never exact.
component.capacitor_electrolytic.failure: Electrolytic capacitor voltage rating exceeded. These can rupture violently when over-volted. Use a cap rated for higher voltage.
Electrolytic capacitor connected backwards. The stripe side (–) must connect toward ground, the plain side (+) toward positive voltage.
component.diode.label: Diode
component.diode.description: Allows current in one direction only. Used for rectification and clipping.
component.diode.model.label: Model
component.diode.model.hint: The real diode part this simulates — sets its forward voltage, leakage, and clipping character automatically.
component.diode.forward_voltage.label: Forward Voltage (V)
component.diode.forward_voltage.hint: The voltage it takes to turn this diode on and let current flow — this is what shapes clipping/distortion character. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.diode.leakage.label: Leakage (IR, µA)
component.diode.leakage.hint: Optional. A tiny amount of current that sneaks through even when the diode is supposed to be off. Usually negligible — leave blank to use the Model's real rating.
component.diode.failure.over_current: Diode current exceeded its maximum rating and it burned out.
component.diode.failure.reverse_voltage: Reverse breakdown voltage exceeded. The diode failed.
component.zener_diode.label: Zener Diode
component.zener_diode.description: Reverse-breakdown voltage regulator. Conducts forward like a normal diode; clamps near a fixed voltage in reverse.
component.zener_diode.model.label: Model
component.zener_diode.model.hint: The real Zener part this simulates — sets its Zener voltage and dynamic impedance automatically.
component.zener_diode.zener_voltage.hint: Optional. The reverse voltage this diode clamps at once it breaks down. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.zener_diode.failure.over_curre: Zener current exceeded its maximum rating and it burned out. Add a series resistor to limit current through the diode.
component.opamp.label: Op-Amp
component.opamp.description: Dual operational amplifier in an 8-pin package. Two independent op-amp units sharing one supply.
component.opamp.model.label: Model
component.opamp.model.hint: The real op-amp chip this simulates — sets its open-loop gain and output swing headroom automatically.
component.opamp.failure.over_voltage: Supply voltage exceeded the chip's rated maximum and it burned out.
component.pt2399.label: PT2399 Delay
component.pt2399.description: 16-pin echo processor IC. Internal delay line with two op-amp stages (OP1 in, OP2 out) for building analog delay/echo pedal circuits.
component.pt2399.failure.over_voltage: Supply voltage exceeded the chip's rated 4.5-5.5V window and it burned out.
component.led.label: LED
component.led.description: Light-emitting diode. Emits light proportional to current.
component.led.color.label: Color
component.led.color.hint: Sets the LED's actual turn-on voltage — different colors need different amounts of voltage to light up.
component.led.forward_voltage.label: Forward Voltage (V)
component.led.forward_voltage.hint: The voltage it takes to turn this LED on. Set automatically by Color — override only for a specific real part.
component.led.max_current_ma.label: Max Current (mA)
component.led.max_current_ma.hint: The most current this LED can safely handle. Always pair an LED with a series resistor to keep current below this.
component.led.failure.over_current: LED burned out from too much current. Always use a current-limiting resistor in series. R = (Vsupply - Vforward) / Imax
component.led.failure.reverse_voltage: Either the LED is installed backwards or the power supply polarity is reversed. The LED's anode (+) should be connected to the positive rail, and the cathode (–) to the negative rail. If the LED is oriented correctly, check that the + and – connections from the power supply haven't been swapped.
component.potentiometer.label: Potentiometer
component.potentiometer.description: Variable resistor with 3 terminals. Wiper position is adjustable.
component.potentiometer.resistance.label: Total Resistance
component.potentiometer.resistance.hint: The pot's full end-to-end resistance — how much total resistance the wiper sweeps across as you turn it.
component.potentiometer.taper.label: Taper
component.potentiometer.taper.hint: How resistance changes as you turn the knob. Linear is even throughout; Audio/Log matches how the ear perceives loudness, common for volume controls.
component.potentiometer.wiper.label: Wiper Position
component.potentiometer.wiper.hint: The knob's current position, from fully counter-clockwise (0) to fully clockwise (1).
component.potentiometer.failure.over_pow: Potentiometer power rating exceeded. Use a lower resistance value or reduce voltage.
component.power_supply.label: DC Power Supply
component.power_supply.description: DC voltage source. Connect + to power rail, – to ground rail.
component.power_supply.power_on.label: Power On
component.power_supply.power_on.hint: Turns this supply on or off, like unplugging the battery.
component.power_supply.voltage.label: Voltage (V)
component.power_supply.voltage.hint: The voltage this supply provides to whatever it's wired into.
The most current this supply can deliver before it can't keep up, like a battery running low under heavy load.
component.power_supply.battery_sag.label: Battery Sag
component.power_supply.battery_sag.hint: How much the voltage dips under load as you play — higher settings mimic a tired battery, audibly compressing and "browning out" on loud playing.
component.power_supply.internal_resistan: How much the supply's own resistance limits current — higher values make Battery Sag more pronounced.
component.signal_generator.label: Signal Generator
component.signal_generator.description: Audio signal source. Choose a waveform or load an audio file.
component.signal_generator.waveform.hint: The shape of the test signal this generator produces.
component.signal_generator.frequency.hin: The pitch of the test tone. A guitar's low E string is about 82Hz; middle A is 440Hz.
component.signal_generator.amplitude.hin: How loud/hard this signal hits the circuit — like picking softly versus digging in.
component.signal_generator.audio_file.hi: Optional. The recorded sample to play when Waveform is set to "Audio File" — has no effect otherwise.
component.switch_spst.label: Switch (SPST)
component.switch_spst.description: Single-pole single-throw switch. On/off. Lives in the External Switches area below the board.
component.switch_spst.type.label: Action
component.switch_spst.type.hint: How the switch behaves when clicked: Latching stays in the new position; Momentary springs back when released (Normally Open = off until held, Normally Closed = on until held).
component.switch_spst.state.label: Initial State
component.switch_spst.state.hint: Whether the switch starts open (circuit broken) or closed (circuit connected) when the board loads.
component.switch_spdt.label: Switch (SPDT)
component.switch_spdt.description: Single-pole double-throw switch. One pole selects between two throws (A/B). Lives in the External Switches area below the board.
component.switch_dpdt.label: Switch (DPDT)
component.switch_dpdt.description: Double-pole double-throw switch. Two poles move together, each selecting between two throws (A/B). Lives in the External Switches area below the board.
component.switch_3pdt.label: Switch (3PDT)
component.switch_3pdt.description: Triple-pole double-throw switch, the standard true-bypass footswitch. Three poles move together, each selecting between two throws (A/B). Lives in the External Switches area below the board.
component.switch_4pdt.label: Switch (4PDT)
component.switch_4pdt.description: Four-pole double-throw switch. Four poles move together, each selecting between two throws (A/B) — used for switching two independent stereo/dual circuits at once. Lives in the External Switches area below the board.
component.switch_mpdt.throw_type.label: Throw Type
component.switch_mpdt.throw_type.hint: On-On: the common always connects to one of the two throws, never neither. On-Off-On: a real neutral middle position connects nothing. (DPDT only) On-On-On: three real positions with no built-in wiring pattern — set it yourself in the Throw Table below, since real on-on-on switches wire differently between manufacturers. Other switch types don't offer On-On-On because real hardware isn't manufactured with that 3-position detent mechanism outside DPDT.
component.switch_mpdt.type.label: Action
component.switch_mpdt.type.hint: Latching stays in whichever position you leave it. Momentary springs back to a rest position when released — Position 1 is rest on On-On (matches real (ON)-(ON) hardware); the center Off position is rest on On-Off-On (matches real (ON)-OFF-(ON) hardware, momentary from either side). Only available for On-On and On-Off-On — On-On-On's per-pole Throw Table has no single rest position to spring back to.
component.switch_mpdt.position.label: Position
component.switch_mpdt.position.hint: Which lever position the switch is currently in. Click the switch itself on the board to change this live — it also updates here.
component.switch_mpdt.throw_table.label: Throw Table (On-On-On)
component.switch_mpdt.throw_table.hint: For each pole, which throw (A/B) is connected at each of the 3 positions. Starts empty on purpose — real on-on-on switches vary by manufacturer, so nothing is assumed here. Check your specific switch's datasheet or test it with a multimeter.
component.transistor_jfet_n.label: N-Channel JFET
component.transistor_jfet_n.description: N-channel junction field-effect transistor. Voltage-controlled: the gate draws no DC current, drain current is set by gate-source voltage.
component.transistor_jfet_n.model.label: Model
component.transistor_jfet_n.model.hint: The real JFET part this simulates — sets its Idss and pinch-off voltage automatically.
component.transistor_jfet_n.idss.label: Idss (Vgs=0 drain current)
component.transistor_jfet_n.idss.hint: Optional. The maximum current this JFET conducts when its gate isn't restricting it at all. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.transistor_jfet_n.vgs_off.hint: Optional. The gate voltage at which this JFET shuts off completely. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.transistor_jfet_n.pinout.label: Pinout
component.transistor_jfet_n.pinout.hint: Which physical leg is Source/Gate/Drain, left to right — matches how the real part's datasheet orders its leads.
component.transistor_jfet_n.failure.over: Drain current exceeded maximum rating. The JFET is destroyed. Check the drain load for too little resistance.
Vds exceeded breakdown voltage. Use a device rated for higher voltage, or reduce the supply.
component.transistor_mosfet_n.label: N-Channel MOSFET
component.transistor_mosfet_n.descriptio: N-channel enhancement-mode MOSFET. Voltage-controlled: the gate draws no DC current, drain current is zero below the gate threshold voltage and rises with the square of gate overdrive above it.
component.transistor_mosfet_n.model.hint: The real MOSFET part this simulates — sets its threshold voltage and transconductance automatically.
component.transistor_mosfet_n.vgs_th.hin: Optional. The gate voltage needed before this MOSFET starts conducting at all. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.transistor_mosfet_n.k.label: k (transconductance coefficient)
component.transistor_mosfet_n.k.hint: Optional. How strongly drain current increases once the gate voltage is past threshold — higher means more gain. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.transistor_mosfet_n.pinout.hin: Which physical leg is Drain/Gate/Source, left to right — matches how the real part's datasheet orders its leads.
component.transistor_mosfet_n.failure.ov: Drain current exceeded maximum rating. The MOSFET is destroyed. Check the drain load for too little resistance.
Vds exceeded breakdown voltage. Use a device rated for higher voltage, or reduce the supply.
component.transistor_npn.label: NPN Transistor
component.transistor_npn.description: NPN bipolar junction transistor. Current-controlled amplifier or switch.
component.transistor_npn.model.label: Model
component.transistor_npn.model.hint: The real transistor part this simulates — sets its gain, saturation voltage, and other ratings automatically.
component.transistor_npn.hfe.label: hFE (gain)
component.transistor_npn.hfe.hint: Optional. How much the base current gets amplified into collector current — higher means more gain. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.transistor_npn.pinout.label: Pinout
component.transistor_npn.pinout.hint: Which physical leg is Emitter/Base/Collector, left to right — matches how the real part's datasheet orders its leads.
component.transistor_npn.leakage.label: Leakage (ICBO)
component.transistor_npn.leakage.hint: Optional. A small current that leaks through even when the transistor is off. Usually tiny for silicon, much larger for germanium — part of what gives old fuzz pedals their character. Leave blank to use the Model's real rating.
component.transistor_npn.failure.over_cu: Collector current exceeded maximum rating. The transistor is destroyed. Add a base resistor to limit current, or use a transistor with a higher current rating.
component.transistor_npn.failure.over_vo: VCE exceeded breakdown voltage. Use a transistor rated for higher voltage.
component.transistor_pnp.label: PNP Transistor
component.transistor_pnp.description: PNP bipolar junction transistor. Current-controlled amplifier or switch — conducts when the base is pulled below the emitter.
component.transistor_pnp.model.label: Model
component.transistor_pnp.model.hint: The real transistor part this simulates — sets its gain, saturation voltage, and other ratings automatically.
component.transistor_pnp.hfe.label: hFE (gain)
component.transistor_pnp.hfe.hint: Optional. How much the base current gets amplified into collector current — higher means more gain. Leave blank to use the selected Model's real rating.
component.transistor_pnp.pinout.label: Pinout
component.transistor_pnp.pinout.hint: Which physical leg is Emitter/Base/Collector, left to right — matches how the real part's datasheet orders its leads.
component.transistor_pnp.leakage.label: Leakage (ICBO)
component.transistor_pnp.leakage.hint: Optional. A small current that leaks through even when the transistor is off. Usually tiny for silicon, much larger for germanium — part of what gives old fuzz pedals their character. Leave blank to use the Model's real rating.
component.transistor_pnp.failure.over_cu: Collector current exceeded maximum rating. The transistor is destroyed. Add a base resistor to limit current, or use a transistor with a higher current rating.
component.transistor_pnp.failure.over_vo: VCE exceeded breakdown voltage. Use a transistor rated for higher voltage.
